entities.summary:
Ottaviano di Poli, a member of the family of the Counts of Poli, was an Italian Roman Catholic Cardinal. Born in the 12th century, Poli rose to prominence as a key figure in the Catholic Church during the medieval period. He played a significant role in shaping the Church's policies and played a crucial part in the selection of popes.

As a member of the powerful family of the Counts of Poli, Ottaviano di Poli was born into a life of nobility and privilege. His family's influence extended across Italy, and Poli's rise to prominence was influenced by his connections to the powerful families of the time.

Poli's significance can be understood through his various roles and contributions to the Catholic Church. As a cardinal, he participated in several important events, including the selection of popes and the Council of Florence. His contributions to the Church's policies had a lasting impact on the course of Catholicism.

Poli's legacy is a testament to the enduring power of the Catholic Church during the medieval period. His influence can still be felt today, and his contributions to the Church's history are a reminder of the importance of the Church's role in shaping the course of human history.

The significance of Ottaviano di Poli's life can be measured in the lasting impact of his contributions to the Catholic Church. His influence on the Church's policies and his role in the selection of popes had a profound impact on the course of Catholicism.

In conclusion, Ottaviano di Poli was a significant figure in the Catholic Church during the medieval period. His contributions to the Church's policies and his role in the selection of popes had a lasting impact on the course of Catholicism.
